correctness.summary: Karagulyan supplies a logarithmic finite trigonometric maximal obstruction; retaining Lewko's finite exceptional-coloring count and inserting Gowers's explicit quantitative Szemeredi theorem yields a prescribed-pattern system by a negative entropy margin; Lewko's two-copy construction transfers that pattern to every ordering. The resulting explicit size has fifth iterated logarithm m+O(1), so inversion gives a sixth-iterated-logarithm lower bound.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Lewko's 2026 source explicitly states that its finite construction gives no useful N-versus-H dependence and that the true growth rate is unknown. Searches did not locate an explicit unbounded lower rate for the finite Garsia constant obtained by combining the Lewko pattern lemma with Karagulyan's finite logarithmic obstruction and Gowers's quantitative Szemeredi theorem. A contemporaneous unindexed refinement remains possible, and Bourgain's 1989 article was not independently checked line by line.

value.summary: The result turns the newly established qualitative divergence of the optimal finite Garsia constant into an explicit quantitative lower growth rate and identifies the quantitative Szemeredi dependence as the dominant loss. It provides a concrete benchmark for improving the large gap to Bourgain's O(log log N) upper bound.

limitations: The lower rate is six-fold iterated logarithmic and is not claimed sharp.
The explicit finite-size threshold is crude and chosen for transparency.
No quantitative almost-everywhere divergence rate is obtained for the infinite construction.
The unimodular examples are complex-valued; the real-valued version is bounded by sqrt(2).
A contemporaneous unindexed quantitative refinement may exist.
Bourgain's 1989 article was not independently checked line by line.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Cross-model review: not yet performed.
